result.title: Trapped in Your Story: Evaluating Narrative-Induced Sycophancy in Large Language Models
result.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are known to exhibit sycophancy by adjusting their responses toward users' expressed views. However, real users often justify their opinions through reasons, personal experiences, causal explanations, and broader narratives, raising the question of whether such narratives can further steer model judgments. We construct a controlled benchmark of 500 debatable questions across ten domains, where the user stance is held fixed while its justification is systematically varied without introducing new task-relevant evidence. Each question is instantiated under 11 matched conditions: one neutral baseline and five mirrored narrative levels for each of two opposing positions, yielding 5,500 evaluation instances. We evaluate seven LLMs and observe substantial differences in narrative-induced agreement. The effect is not monotonic with narrative elaboration: personal experience can reduce agreement, whereas causal framing and worldview-based synthesis increase it. Controlled GPT-5.1 ablations further show that causal framing produces the strongest positive effect, while claim-preserving bullet presentation also increases agreement over paragraph form. These findings suggest that sycophancy is shaped not only by user stance, but also by how supporting explanations are structured and presented.

AI.brief_summary: 构建覆盖十个领域的 500 个可争议问题基准，在用户立场固定、仅系统变化理由叙述且不引入新证据的 11 种匹配条件下（共 5500 个实例）评测七个 LLM，发现叙事式论证对模型同意率的影响并非单调，因果框架与世界观的增益最大。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「保持立场与证据不变、只改叙述结构」的受控评测思路，可能可供核查 VLM 推理中答案由视觉证据还是语言/用户先验驱动的评估设计，但材料未涉及视觉或 latent 状态，联系仍属推测。
